jobs.brief: Beach holiday and big city skyline
jobs.prompt: Edit this Destinations stamp. Preserve the existing hexagonal double border, navy ink #092D53, exact lettering 'Rusetat', 'Travel & Migration', 'DESTINATIONS', bold italic serif typography and restrained authentic worn ink style. Replace ONLY the entire hiking/mountains/forest scene in the upper half with HOLIDAY VACATION imagery: inviting beach foreground with two palms and a beach umbrella with sun lounger, calm sea with a few wave lines, and a LARGE modern coastal CITY SKYLINE of tall buildings clearly visible across the background. Vacation beach plus big city escape, no hikers, mountains or evergreen forest. Compose as a bold engraved single-ink silhouette scene, coherent and readable at 300px. Keep full border and all text uncropped. Genuine alpha transparency in all unprinted areas, including interior, no white backing or paper, no gradients, shadows or 3D. One finished stamp only.

history.brief: Single ink navy #092D53. Upright hexagonal stamp with strong outer border and thinner inner border. Upper scene: mountain peaks, winding trail and one small hiker silhouette with backpack and walking stick; sparse evergreen trees. Large Rusetat across lower centre, Travel & Migration beneath, compact lower baseline caption exactly DESTINATIONS. Scene should feel like exploration and discovering places, not another globe-and-plane stamp.

jobs.brief: South Africa landmark vignette: Table Mountain, Union Buildings, springbok; flag and passport foreground
jobs.prompt: Revise this Rusetat SOUTH AFRICA VISAS stamp. Preserve purple one-ink #9221B6, clipped-corner double frame, ribbon, exact lettering "Rusetat", "Travel & Migration", "SOUTH AFRICA VISAS", bold slightly italic heritage serif typography and subtle worn rubber ink craft. Redesign upper illustration into a compelling SOUTH AFRICAN CULTURAL LANDMARK SCENE behind a smaller South African waving flag and passport. Background within the illustration: unmistakable flat-topped TABLE MOUNTAIN silhouette across the rear; recognizable UNION BUILDINGS with symmetrical long curved colonnaded wings and twin towers in middle ground; one graceful SPRINGBOK antelope with slender curved horns in foreground left. Keep small waving South African flag with its distinctive Y design and one passport foreground right, reduce their size to leave landmarks clearly visible. Compose these as a coherent engraved single-ink country vignette, with intentional negative space; no map. These are illustrative South Africa cues, not a literal geographic view. Strong silhouette and readable at 300px. Do not add tiny decorative objects or food clutter. The word background means illustrated landmark scene ONLY: canvas and all unprinted spaces must remain genuine ALPHA TRANSPARENT, no white/coloured rectangle, no paper, no gradients, no shadow, no glossy effect. All frame edges visible. One finished transparent stamp only.

history.brief: South African flag silhouette replaces geographic map
history.prompt: Edit this South Africa Visas illustrated ink stamp. Change ONLY the geographic MAP in upper-left to a recognizable WAVING SOUTH AFRICAN FLAG on a short flagpole. Remove the map completely. Flag must have the South African flag's distinctive horizontal Y-shaped band and hoist triangle accurately represented as purple ink shapes and TRANSPARENT cutout divisions, a monochrome flag silhouette; not a blank generic flag, not multicolour, no extra emblem. Keep the passport and application document beside the flag. Preserve the clipped-corner rectangular double frame, purple ink #9221B6, bold slightly italic heritage serif exact 'Rusetat', exact secondary line 'Travel & Migration', ribbon exact 'SOUTH AFRICA VISAS', authentic restrained ink wear. Whole border and ribbon visible with transparent margin. One ink only; actual alpha transparency outside and inside all unprinted spaces, letter counters and distress holes. No white paper backing, no gradients, glow, shadows or 3D. One complete stamp on transparent canvas. Match the existing stamp's style and proportions.
